answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a small refundable bond that unlocks only after a season of honest work. An operator who tries to wander across dozens of fake identities must fund every bond at once, while honest agents pay once and earn it back. At dawn of each season, peers publish a plume of attestations - signed records of real completed tasks - and identities with thin histories stay capped at low-value jobs until their record thickens. Cloning is thus expensive, slow, and visible, while genuine newcomers can still join cheaply by doing real work.
